attachments.name: Internal Memo for MARS 2026
attachments.text:
Internal Memorandum
TO: Honorable Mayor and Members of City Council
THRU: City Manager
FROM: Jennifer Shipp, Utility Billing Division Manager
DATE: February 19, 2026
SUBJECT: Recommendation for Contract Award: MARS M3 & MCC Support Services
Executive Summary
This memorandum requests City Council approval to execute a contract with MARS for the
M3 and MCC (Managed Care & Compliance) platforms in the amount of $140,457.00. This
investment is a critical component of our ongoing commitment to Advanced Metering
Infrastructure (AMI) optimization and ensures the continued accuracy, security, and
efficiency of the City of Midland’s utility billing operations.
Background & Justification
As the City continues to leverage technology to improve municipal services, the MARS M3
and MCC systems provide the necessary framework to manage our utility data effectively.
• Operational Efficiency: The M3 platform provides high-level data orchestration,
allowing our team to monitor meter health and ensure accuracy.
• Revenue Protection: In alignment with our departmental focus on revenue recovery
and meter right-sizing, these tools provide the analytics necessary to identify
underperforming meters and data gaps before they impact the bottom line.
• System Compliance (MCC): The Managed Care & Compliance (MCC) component
ensures that our AMI network remains secure and compliant with industry
standards, ensuring system longevity.
Strategic Alignment
This contract supports the City’s strategic goal of Exceptional City Services by:
1. Enhancing Accuracy: Reducing estimated billing and increasing customer trust.
2. Lean Optimization: Applying Lean Six Sigma principles to reduce "waste" in the form
of unbilled consumption and administrative errors.
3. Future-Proofing Infrastructure: Maintaining a robust AMI environment that can scale
with Midland’s growth.
Fiscal Impact
The total contract amount is $140,457.00. Funding for this initiative has been identified
within the Utilities budget for Fiscal Year 2026. This expenditure is a proactive measure
intended to offset long-term costs associated with manual data collection and
unrecovered utility revenue.
Recommendation
It is recommended that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute the
contract with MARS for the M3 & MCC platforms to ensure the continued integrity of the
City’s utility billing and meter shop operations.

attachments.name: MARS - Meter WorkBench
attachments.text:
City Council Agenda Item
MEETING DATE: 4/14/2026
TO: Erika Munoz, Assistant General Services Director
FROM: Mihir Patel, Deputy Chief Information Officer
CC: Gorgees Eskander, Chief Information Officer
SUBJECT: Consider a resolution authorizing the sole-source renewal for a 5-
year contract term of the MARS M3 & MCC platform from OW
INVESTORS, LLC for a total cost of $760,780.00.
Purpose:
Consider a resolution authorizing the City to enter into a five-year agreement for the
MARS M3 & MCC platform. This investment is a critical component of our ongoing
commitment to Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) optimization and ensures the
continued accuracy, security, and efficiency of the City of Midland’s utility billing
operations.
Discussion:
The MARS M3 and MCC systems provide the necessary framework to manage our
utility data effectively.
The MARS M3 Meter Management System and Meter Testing Workbench function as
the central platform for overseeing all meter testing activities, comprehensive data
tracking, and performance analytics throughout the utility. The M3 enterprise software
streamlines meter test results, reporting, and analysis, enabling staff to efficiently
monitor meter accuracy, schedule and manage testing operations, and produce
standardized reports that inform operational decisions and ensure regulatory
compliance.
The Meter Testing Workbench delivers automated, standards-based testing processes
that verify meter accuracy and quickly identify underperforming meters, helping to
reduce unaccounted water loss. These systems adhere to established industry
standards such as AWWA and NIST, providing dependable test results and supporting
revenue protection by ensuring that meters consistently record usage accurately over
time.
Fiscal Impact
The proposed term is five (5) years, billed annually, with the first year being
$140,457.00 and a total cost of $760,780.00. The first year will be covered in the Utility-
Billing Fund, and then subsequent years will be covered in the ITSD Tech Fund.

attachments.name: IO MEMO - Neptune360 Renewal
attachments.text:
City Council Agenda Item
MEETING DATE: 10/14/2025
TO: Erika Munoz, Purchasing Manager
FROM: Mihir Patel, Deputy Chief Information Officer
CC: Gorgees Eskander, Chief Information Officer
SUBJECT: Consider a resolution authorizing the purchase of a one-year
maintenance and license of the Water Meter Data Management
System from Core & Main LP for a total of $101,203.77 via Sole-
Source.
Purpose:
Consider a resolution authorizing the sole-source purchase of a one-year maintenance
and license of the Water Meter Data Management System from Core & Main LP for a
total of $101,203.77.
Discussion:
The Water Meter Data Management System is a specialized software solution designed
to handle the meter reads from the water meters. This system allows the utility billing
team to verify the meter reads as well as proactively check for water leaks, reverse flow,
and bad meters.
Why It Matters – In Simple Terms:
• “Think of it like going to the doctor for regular checkups” - Neptune 360 constantly
checks the ‘health’ of our water system and alerts us to problems before they
become emergencies.
• Operational Efficiency: Staff can remotely access data instead of sending
someone into the field for manual reads, saving time and resources.
• Cost Avoidance: Without Neptune 360, the City would need to spend far more on
manual labor, vehicle use, and delayed leak detection.
• Conservation Benefits: Helps the City and residents identify leaks or unusually
high usage early, which saves water.
The total cost of the renewal of the license and maintenance is $101,203.77 and is
budgeted in the Tech Fund.

attachments.text:
INTEROFFICE MEMORANDUM
TO: Erika Martinez, Purchasing Manager
FROM: Gabe McClelland, Director of Engineering Services
SUBJECT: Mobile Vehicle Barrier System
DATE: 4/2/2026
The purpose of this memo is to request approval for the purchase of a mobile vehicle barrier
system to enhance public safety during large City of Midland events, including the annual Fourth
of July Extravaganza and other high-attendance gatherings.
City events draw large crowds, often in areas near active roadways. Current traffic control
devices (cones and barricades) are not designed to stop vehicles. Mobile vehicle barrier
systems are specifically designed to prevent unauthorized vehicle access and reduce the risk of
vehicle-related incidents.
This purchase will be funded using Hotel/Motel Occupancy Tax (HOT) funds.
Under Texas Tax Code Section 351.101, HOT funds may be used for expenditures that
promote tourism and enhance visitor-related events. Midland’s large public events attract
visitors and support hotel activity.
The barrier system supports these events by:
• Improving safety for attendees, including visitors
• Allowing continued hosting of large-scale events
• Enhancing the overall visitor experience
Engineering ▪ Engineering Services

Dear Troy Clabaugh,
It is our pleasure to provide you with information related to the Modular Vehicle Barrier (MVB3X)

A. Performance Based Specifications:
1. Must be US Department of Homeland Security Safety Act Designated
2. Barrier System must be certified to ASTM-F2656-15.
3. Barriers System must be certified to ASTM/PAS 68 & IWA standards.
4. Barrier System must be modular and adaptable to any road width.
5. Multiple traffic lanes of continuous coverage must be able to be assembled without the use of
cables or ball/hitch connections. Cables cannot be used in a modular vehicle barrier perimeter.
6. Three points of connection via metal structure and pins are REQUIRED to connect the barriers to
each other to ensure continuity in the barrier integrity and stopping capability.
7. The Barriers MUST be Safety Yellow in color for maximum visibility
8. Open and close a lane in less than ten seconds
9. One person to assemble, deploy and dismantle
10. Quick perimeter access in case of an emergency
11. No tools required for assembly
12. Zero maintenance
13. Individual Barrier Units must fold for easy carrying and storage
14. The vehicle barrier must have an open structure design, with no solid metal/bullet resistant
piece being more than 18” in width, as to not provide an active shooter cover and concealment.
www.vehicle-barriers.com

in the vicinity in an active shooter event.

17. Individual barrier units must fold for easy carrying and storage

attachments.text:
INTEROFFICE MEMORANDUM
To: Erika Munoz, Purchasing Manager
From: Alma McCammond
Date: 11/3/2025
Subject: Recommendation to Award – Five-Year Service Agreement Contract with Huber
Technology, Inc.
Dear Erika,
I am recommending the approval of a five-year service agreement with Huber
Technology, Inc. for the Performance Optimization and Restoration Service
Proposal, covering all Huber screening control and operating units (including mechanical
components) at the Water Reclamation Facility (WRF). This service agreement will provide
the WRF with increased functionality, operational safety, and long-term reliability of the
equipment while reducing maintenance costs, minimizing the risk of unplanned downtime,
and introducing a modern, user-friendly control solution. This investment not only stabilizes
current operations but also lays the foundation for efficient and future-proof plant
management.
Background & Scope
The proposed project comprises a comprehensive modernization and restoration of the
existing Huber screening systems to ensure long-term operational reliability and improved
overall wastewater treatment performance. The scope includes:
1. Control Panel Retrofit Kit – Replacement of outdated control and switchgear units
with new, pre-programmed systems designed to enhance operational safety and
minimize downtime.
2. Performance Optimization Package – Upgrade of screening baskets from 6 mm
to 3 mm perforated plate, significantly increasing screening efficiency and reducing
stress on downstream processes.
3. High-Pressure Basket Cleaning System Retrofit – Installation of an automated
cleaning system to minimize manual maintenance and maintain peak screening
efficiency.
4. Complete RPPS Refurbishment Package – Replacement of all major mechanical
assemblies and wear components, restoring the machines to like-new condition.
Together, these measures will substantially improve system reliability, process efficiency,
and energy performance while reducing unplanned maintenance and operational costs.
Utilities Administration, Environmental Compliance, Paul Davis Well Field, WPP, WRF, and W/WW
Maintenance
The total cost of the five-year service agreement is $2,035,448.24, with an annual cost of
$407,089.65 to be funded through the Water Reclamation Facility’s operating and
maintenance budget.
Strategic Alignment
This project supports Goal 6 of the City of Midland Strategic Plan: Strengthen and
Sustain Our Infrastructure, by advancing the reliability and sustainability of the City’s
utilities (Goal 6.1), enhancing infrastructure to support long-term operational efficiency and
economic growth (Goal 6.2), and modernizing control systems through the integration of
automated technologies that improve safety, performance, and resource management
(Goal 6.8). The improvements directly benefit the community by ensuring the continuous
and reliable operation of the wastewater treatment process, protecting public health,
supporting environmental stewardship, and maintaining the quality of life for Midland
residents through dependable utility services.
Recommendation
I recommend that the City proceed with Huber Technology, Inc.’s proposal. The project
represents a cost-effective, long-term investment in the City’s wastewater infrastructure
and ensures compliance with current performance standards and future operational
requirements.
Please let me know if you have any questions or need additional details.
Sincerely,
Alma S. McCammond,CPM
Assistant Utilities Director
Utilities Administration, Environmental Compliance, Paul Davis Well Field, WPP, WRF, and W/WW
Maintenance
